title: feat(pm-sentinel-tick): real, automated, per-tick zero-LLM-token guard (UMR-20260813-102459-10c3)
body:
task-20260814-054352-actually-implement-the-server-native-pm

## REAL FINDING (verified from scratch, not trusted from prior doc claims)

The dispatching SPEC claimed the 10c3 collapse (sentinel tick +
financial-escalation policy + hierarchy/single-gateway policy into ONE
script) was "merged-audit-passed on paper" via a claude-control PR whose
only changed file was a status report, zero real code landed.

Independently re-checked:
- PR #298 ("collapse ... into ONE script (10c3)") is real code (696 lines)
  but **CLOSED, not merged** -- its own comment says superseded by #299.
- PR #299 ("integrate UMR-102459-10c3 + query-once/decide-and-fix") **is
  merged** to `main` (`ae48cf0`) and really did carry #298's content
  forward -- confirmed `git merge-base --is-ancestor ae48cf0 main`. Current
  `main` `pm-sentinel-tick.sh` (1084 lines) has real, working
  `is_financial_decision()`/`escalate_financial_decision()`, dynamic
  addenda-chain discovery, `emit_report_row()` boolean-table JSONL,
  Prometheus metrics, and the base sentinel-tick RCA dispatch. Further real
  fixes on top: PR #323 (`7dac937`), PR #341 (`f9b4101`).

So by the time this task ran, the 3-piece collapse was already real, on
`main`, with a real passing test suite -- not something to redo from zero.

## Real gap this PR actually fixes

`pm-sentinel-tick.sh`'s own "TOKEN USAGE" header comment claimed zero LLM
calls "verified by grep" and pointed to `PROGRESS.md` for "the real measured
before/after token comparison" -- a one-time manual claim, never
automatically re-checked, and no `PROGRESS.md` snapshot in this repo's
history actually contained that comparison. A future edit could add a real
LLM call here and the doc comment would keep silently claiming zero.

Real fix:
- `LLM_INVOCATION_PATTERN` + `assert_zero_llm_token_usage()`
  (`pm-sentinel-tick.sh`): narrow real call-site regex (same convention as
  the existing `FINANCIAL_KEYWORDS`), strips comment lines, greps real code
  for an actual LLM invocation call site, fails the tick loudly (non-zero
  exit, same `TICK_FAILURES` convention every other real tick failure
  already uses) if one is ever introduced. Runs first thing every real
  tick.
- `pm_sentinel_tick_llm_invocation_count` Prometheus gauge: real,
  continuously re-measured token-delta baseline (0 by contract), exposed
  every hourly tick.
- `PmSentinelTickTokenZeroGuardTest` (`test_pm_sentinel_tick.py`, 2 real
  tests): (1) the real shipped script passes its own guard; (2) a mutated
  copy with one real LLM call site appended (`curl
  https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`) is caught -- proves the guard is a
  real detector, not a tautology.
- `PROGRESS.md`: real measured token-delta record + the #298/#299
  supersession verification trail above.

## Real files changed
- `pm-sentinel-tick.sh`
- `test_pm_sentinel_tick.py`
- `PROGRESS.md`

## Real test run

```
python3 -m pytest test_pm_sentinel_tick.py -v
================= 13 passed =================
```
13 tests (11 pre-existing + 2 new), real isolated sqlite3 COPY of the live
Superboss Register DB (backup API, never the live DB), real
`dispatch-owner-task.sh --no-relay` subprocess calls.

`bash -n pm-sentinel-tick.sh`: syntax OK.
`python3 -m py_compile test_pm_sentinel_tick.py`: OK.

title: fix(disk-exhaustion): stop test harnesses leaking ~4GB register copies to /tmp (UMR-20260814-033442-c885)
body:
## P0 RCA: disk exhaustion caused by leaked test-harness scratch (UMR-20260814-033442-c885)

Cites UMR-20260814-010802-b566 only as a **victim** task (killed by preflight `disk_low`), not the cause.

### Symptom (real evidence, PM-Desktop Sentinel, 2026-08-14 03:1x UTC)
`/dev/sda1` hit **288G used / 96MB free (100% full)**. Every `veridian-worker` unit died at preflight (`disk_low`), all 17 running units failed, `resource_governor.py --query-umr` returned `count=0` for every real status — the whole AI OS halted.

### Root cause (measured, `du -sx -m`)
`/tmp` held **2996 entries, ~122GB**, almost entirely leaked test-harness scratch:
- 21× `pm_sentinel_tick_*` = 74.5GB
- 118× `rule7-real-persist-test-*` / `rule7-non-completed-test-*`
- 11× `rg_queue_mgmt_test_*` = 15.2GB
- standalone `sbr-test-copy.sqlite`/`dedup_test.sqlite`/`test.sqlite` copies (~3.8GB each)

Each scratch dir was ~4-6GB because the harness copied the **entire ~3.9GB `superboss-register.sqlite`** and never removed it.

### Before / after disk state
- **Before** (Sentinel's real measurement, incident time): 288G used / 96MB free / **100%**
- **After Sentinel's own emergency mitigation** (already done before this task started, not repeated here): 189G used / 100G free / 66%
- **Current** (`df -h /` at PR time, after all fixes + full test runs in this PR): `301G 189G 99G 66% /`
- **Per-test-copy size, before vs. after this fix** (the real root cause, not just the leak):
  ```
  Live DB:            3044.30 MB
  OLD (src.backup):   ~3044 MB copied per test invocation
  NEW (schema-only):     0.95 MB copied per test invocation
  ```
  ~3200x reduction. This is the actual defect fix — cleanup alone still meant ~4GB of disk churn per test run.

### Fixes (all 4 required parts)

**1. Stop copying the whole register.** `test_pm_sentinel_tick.py` and `test_resource_governor_queue_management.py`: `src.backup(dst)` (full sqlite3 binary backup) → a real schema-only clone (every table/index/trigger/view definition from `sqlite_master`, zero row data). These tests only ever read back rows they seed themselves — never live data. Three-pass copy (virtual tables → ordinary tables → indexes/triggers/views): a naive single-pass rowid-ordered copy silently left `umr_tasks_fts` never actually created, because FTS5 shadow-table rows can have **lower** `sqlite_master` rowids than their own owning virtual table on this DB (confirmed live, not theoretical — caught this via a real 12-test failure before fixing the ordering).

**2. Make cleanup unconditional, not happy-path-only.**
- `tests/test_rule7_completion_evidence.py`: two `tempfile.mkdtemp()` scratch dirs were **never removed at all** — a 100%-leak-rate bug (every run, pass or fail), the confirmed real defect behind those 118 leaked dirs. Fixed via `finally: shutil.rmtree(...)`.
- `test_pm_sentinel_tick.py` / `test_resource_governor_queue_management.py`: `tearDown()`'s own `rmtree` never ran if `setUp()` itself raised (e.g. mid-copy on a disk-full box — the exact failure mode this incident created). Fixed via `self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, ...)` registered immediately after `mkdtemp`, which unittest guarantees runs even when `setUp()` raises afterward.

**Real proof, not just a passing run:** sabotaged one assertion in each of the three files to force a genuine test **failure**, ran it, confirmed the `AssertionError` fired **and** zero scratch dirs remained under `/tmp` afterward, then reverted the sabotage. Example (rule7):
```
E    assert 'in_progress' == 'DELIBERATELY...FORCE-FAILURE'
1 failed in 0.89s
--- scratch dirs remaining under /tmp after the FAILING test ---
0
```
All three real, unmodified suites pass clean:
```
test_pm_sentinel_tick.py ................. 11 passed in 31-33s
tests/test_rule7_completion_evidence.py ... 14 passed in 0.7-0.9s
test_resource_governor_queue_management.py  13 passed in 5.7-7.5s
```

**3. `reap_stale_test_scratch.py`** — new periodic backstop. Removes stale (>2h, configurable) `/tmp` entries matching the real confirmed leak prefixes/filenames from this RCA (`pm_sentinel_tick_`, `rule7-real-persist-test-`, `rule7-non-completed-test-`, `rg_queue_mgmt_test_`, `sbr-test-copy.sqlite`, `dedup_test.sqlite`). Best-effort `lsof` open-handle check before deleting. Never touches anything outside `/tmp`, never a bare wildcard sweep. 3/3 new tests pass (`tests/test_reap_stale_test_scratch.py`). Wired to a new systemd `--user` timer (`systemd/veridian-cron-reap-stale-test-scratch.{service,timer}`, 30-min cadence) — **tracked reference copy only, not yet deployed live**, same convention as every other file in `systemd/` (see that `.service` file's header for the closed-set authorization disclosure).

**4. journald/logrotate caps** for the second unbounded grower on the same volume (`config/host/`, tracked reference copies, **not yet deployed live** — this session had no passwordless `sudo`). Real measured before-state: journald 3.6G disk usage with `SystemMaxUse` unset (commented out); `/var/log/syslog` 7510MB + `syslog.1` 1552MB with `weekly, rotate 4` and **no size cap at all**. `journald.conf.d` drop-in adds `SystemMaxUse=1G`. `logrotate.d/rsyslog` adds `maxsize 500M` (mutually exclusive with `size` per `man logrotate`, so this augments the existing weekly cadence rather than replacing it) to the real, byte-identical live stanza.

### Separately (claude-control repo, not this PR)
`preflight-guard.py`'s `check_disk()` now calls `notify-owner.py` (rate-limited 1/hour via its own `dedupe_key`) before rejecting on `disk_low`, so a repeat of "17 units failed silently, no alert until a human found it by hand" now sends a real email. Verified via a monkeypatched smoke test (disk_usage faked to 100MB free, `notify-owner.py` invocation captured and asserted before the `SystemExit`).

### Known, pre-existing, out-of-scope finding
`test_resource_governor_queue_management.py`'s `_write_lock()` usage resolves to the **live** `/opt/veridian/ai-os/memory/superboss-register.sqlite.writelock` — `resource_governor.py`'s `_WRITE_LOCK_PATH` is computed once at module-import time from the default `DB_PATH`, before the test overrides `sbr.DB_PATH` to its own isolated copy. Confirmed via `fuser` showing 7-9 real live PIDs contending on that exact lock file while this suite ran, causing genuine multi-minute hangs under live load (unrelated to this PR's changes — reproduced identically against the pre-existing, unmodified file). Not fixed here (test-isolation bug in the write-lock path, orthogonal to the disk-leak root cause) — flagged for a follow-up, not silently left undocumented.

title: fix(worker-entrypoint): stop charging lifetime invocation counter for preflight rejections
body:
## Real defect (confirmed live, PM Sentinel, 2026-08-14)

`worker-entrypoint.sh` (ExecStart of the templated `veridian-worker@.service`
unit) charged its lifetime invocation counter (`.invocation_count`, capped at
`MAX_LIFETIME_INVOCATIONS=20`) **before** the preflight guard ran. A purely
infrastructural preflight rejection (`disk_low`, `memory_low`, worktree
contention, ...) -- which never calls the model, costs $0, and produces zero
output -- still permanently burned a lifetime invocation slot. systemd's
`Restart=on-failure` then retried up to `StartLimitBurst=3` times, each
charging another slot for zero real work.

**Real proof this was not theoretical**: a host-level full-volume event on
2026-08-14 rejected 11 distinct tasks with guard reason `disk_low`. One
(`task-20260718-171007-commercial--subscription---pricing-model`) was already
at 18/20 lifetime invocations despite never having executed a single real
model call -- two more infra hiccups from being permanently, silently
unrunnable for a condition it had zero power to affect.

## Fix

1. **The lifetime invocation counter is now written only once preflight has
   passed and a real model call is imminent** (new
   `LIFETIME-INVOCATION-CHARGE-BLOCK`, immediately after
   `PREFLIGHT-GUARD-BLOCK-END`). Neither the preflight hard-stop branch nor
   the transient branch ever reaches it. Invariant: this counter now reflects
   REAL model invocations only.
2. **A new, separate `.infra_rejection_count` counter** bounds the
   transient/infrastructural preflight-rejection path on its own budget
   (`MAX_INFRA_REJECTIONS`, default 5, env-overridable via
   `VERIDIAN_MAX_INFRA_REJECTIONS`), with its own growing backoff
   (`sleep $((count * 5))`). Once exceeded, the unit is disabled and stops
   retrying -- same shape as the existing hard-stop branch -- so a genuinely
   broken host still cannot spin a task forever, without ever again borrowing
   from the real model-invocation budget to provide that protection.

## Real repair of already-damaged counters

Separately (data repair, not part of this diff -- tracked in the dispatching
task's own workspace/progress file): all 11 real tasks named above had their
`.invocation_count` corrected, derived from each task's own `task.yaml`
checkpoint history (discounting checkpoints whose note contains
`-- no model call made, no cost incurred`), with a full before/after table.

## Real test -- run, not self-certified

`tests/preflight_guard_hardstop_test.sh` extracts the REAL
`PREFLIGHT-GUARD-BLOCK` + `LIFETIME-INVOCATION-CHARGE-BLOCK` verbatim from
this file's own text (the file the sed range comment `tests/
preflight_guard_hardstop_test.sh extracts this` already promised) and runs it
as a real bash subprocess, with only `python3`/`systemctl`/`sleep` shimmed via
`PATH`. A change to the real block is picked up automatically -- there is no
separate reimplementation of the guard logic to keep in sync.

Real, pasted output (`bash tests/preflight_guard_hardstop_test.sh`, exit code
`0`):

```
=== Test 1: a single transient (infra) preflight rejection must NOT charge the lifetime invocation counter ===
PASS: transient rejection exits 1 (systemd retries) (got '1')
PASS: lifetime invocation counter file was never created
PASS: infra rejection counter is now 1 (got '1')
PASS: checkpoint note says lifetime counter NOT charged
PASS: checkpoint status is failed, not blocked
PASS: backoff sleep was invoked (5s for 1st infra rejection)

=== Test 2: repeated infra rejections increment their OWN counter, back off, and eventually stop retrying -- all while the lifetime counter stays untouched ===
PASS: attempt 1: still under cap, exits 1 (retryable) (got '1')
PASS: attempt 1: infra counter is 1 (got '1')
PASS: attempt 1: lifetime counter still never created
PASS: attempt 2: still under cap, exits 1 (retryable) (got '1')
PASS: attempt 2: infra counter is 2 (got '2')
PASS: attempt 2: lifetime counter still never created
PASS: attempt 3: still under cap, exits 1 (retryable) (got '1')
PASS: attempt 3: infra counter is 3 (got '3')
PASS: attempt 3: lifetime counter still never created
PASS: infra cap exceeded (4 > 3): exits 0, systemd will NOT retry (got '0')
PASS: infra counter is now 4 (past its own cap) (got '4')
PASS: lifetime counter STILL never created after infra cap hit
PASS: unit was disabled once infra cap hit (stops retrying)
PASS: checkpoint records INFRASTRUCTURE-REJECTION CAP HIT
PASS: backoff grew across attempts (5s, 10s, 15s)
PASS: backoff grew across attempts (5s, 10s, 15s)
PASS: backoff grew across attempts (5s, 10s, 15s)

=== Test 3: a hard-stop preflight reason (deterministic, e.g. circuit_breaker_tripped) also never charges the lifetime counter ===
PASS: hard stop exits 0 (systemd will not retry, unit disabled) (got '0')
PASS: hard stop never charges the lifetime invocation counter
PASS: hard stop never touches the infra-rejection counter either
PASS: checkpoint records PRE-FLIGHT HARD STOP
PASS: unit was disabled

=== Test 4: once preflight PASSES, the lifetime invocation counter IS charged (a real model call is imminent) ===
PASS: preflight pass falls through the block with exit 0 (script continues below) (got '0')
PASS: lifetime invocation counter is now 1 (charged exactly once preflight passed) (got '1')
PASS: infra rejection counter untouched on a clean pass

=== Test 5: MAX_LIFETIME_INVOCATIONS cap check (unrelated to this fix, must still work) is unaffected -- PRIOR_COUNT>=MAX still hard-stops without incrementing further ===
PASS: at 20/20 prior invocations, cap check exits 0 before doing anything else (got '0')
PASS: cap check correctly stopped script execution (exit, not fall-through)
PASS: invocation count file is untouched at exactly 20 (no further charge) (got '20')

================================================================
RESULTS: 34 passed, 0 failed
================================================================
```

Test 1 satisfies "simulates a transient preflight rejection and asserts the
lifetime counter is UNCHANGED". Test 2 satisfies "asserts the new
infrastructure counter does increment and does eventually stop retrying".
Tests 3-5 are additional real coverage for adjacent invariants this fix
touches (hard-stop paths, the pass-through charge path, and the pre-existing
cap check).

`bash -n worker-entrypoint.sh` also passes (syntax check).

## Scope

Did NOT touch `doc-worker-entrypoint.sh` (separate template,
`veridian-docworker@.service`), host disk usage, logging/journald config, or
dedup/duplicate-guard logic -- all out of scope for this fix.

title: fix(resource_governor): duplicate guards over-block brand-new/resumed work (UMR-20260814-010950)
body:
Governing chain: P1 UMR-20260806-171945-5767. Task: UMR-20260814-010944-2e16
(task-20260814-010950-duplicate-guard-over-blocks--a-brand-new).

## Real problem

Two independent, real, over-broad duplicate guards in `resource_governor.py` were
silently killing brand-new/resumed legitimate dispatches (`ts_dispatched=NULL`, never
spawned).

### 1. `find_pr_for_task_identity()` Stage 6 -- cross-repo / non-target PR-number match

Reproduced live 2026-08-14T01:01:52Z: `UMR-20260814-010152-7981`
(`task_identity='owner-task-20260814-010149-432146'`, brand-new, zero prior branches)
titled *"...every audited merged fix (incl PR 322) is NOT running"* was rejected citing
`FChecklist/claude-control#185`, whose real title is *"Resolve conflict, audit and land
veridian-scripts PR 322..."* -- an unrelated PR in a different repo that merely cites the
same number. The blocked task had to be re-dispatched with the PR number stripped from
its title purely to evade this guard (`UMR-20260814-010802-b566`) -- not acceptable as a
standing requirement.

**Fix:** resolve the title's PR-number reference the same repo-scoped way
`target_pr_already_resolved()` already does (UMR-20260813-165620-aac7) -- prefer a
repo-qualified reference and search only that repo; a bare number is resolved only
against `hint_repo`, never scanned across `GH_PR_CHECK_REPOS`. New
`_title_pr_reference_is_citation_only()` also drops a parenthetical citation entirely
(mirrors the existing `_DISCLOSURE_CITATION_RE` fix, applied to the query side).

### 2. `_orchestrator_reuse_verdict_gate()` -- task/resume intent vs `wiring_registry` file

Real quantified damage, last 7 days (`umr_tasks`, live DB): **474 of 489**
`status=rejected_duplicate` rows -- **all** `systemctl_action` task-resume rows, **all**
never spawned -- were rejected with `best_match={'source': 'wiring_registry', 'kind':
'file'}`. Confirmed: `UMR-20260814-004301-2d07` scored 0.953 against wiring_registry row
`file-10d3faee408e`, which is that **same task's own** prior `task.yaml`. Resuming an
existing unit can never "duplicate" a wiring_registry file by construction.

**Fix:** `_orchestrator_reuse_verdict_gate()` now only runs for
`task_kind=='veridian_task_create'` rows, mirroring the scoping Stage 4/5/6 already
apply just above it.

## Damage, quantified (last 7 days, `umr_tasks`, `status=rejected_duplicate`)

| | count |
|---|---|
| total rejected_duplicate | 489 |
| never spawned (`ts_dispatched IS NULL`) | 485 |
| via duplicate-PR guard (Stage 4/5/6) | 6 (all 6 had `prior real branch(es) []` -- all false positives via Stage 6 only) |
| via reuse_verdict_engine duplication_blocked | 474 (all 474 `best_match.kind=='file'`, all never spawned) |

## Tests

`tests/test_duplicate_guard_over_broad_false_positives.py` -- 8 new tests, real
mocked-`_run()` / isolated scratch-sqlite, no network, no live DB:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_duplicate_guard_over_broad_false_positives.py -v
8 passed in 0.39s
```

Full regression suite after the fix:

```
$ python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
707 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (test_timer_is_really_enabled_and_active --
environment systemd-timer check, present on origin/main before this branch)
```

## Do NOT merge without

A fresh, independent Tier-1 `AUDIT:PASS` comment on this PR's head SHA.

title: docs: RCA for UMR-20260807-101751-68ff (killed) -- honest self-withdrawal, no fix needed
body:
## Summary

RCA for `UMR-20260807-101751-68ff` (status=`killed`), per this task's dispatching SPEC.

**Root cause: not a bug** -- an honest, correctly-reasoned PM self-withdrawal. The UMR dispatched PR #249 review/merge/deploy work at 10:17 UTC on 2026-08-07. 41 minutes later the PM read the Owner absolute stop-work order verbatim for the first time and found it explicitly named "any PR review or push work" as paused. It withdrew rather than rationalize an exception, and recorded the reasoning honestly, naming PR #249 as still OPEN/MERGEABLE and nothing lost.

**Verified correct at the time**: the stop-work order (`UMR-20260806-124055-bc80`) was genuinely live on 2026-08-07T10:58 UTC and was only lifted the next day (2026-08-08, commit `ca513ca2`). `status=killed` is an accurate historical record, not a mislabel to correct.

**Verified the deferred scope is now closed**, by later independent dispatches:
- PR #249 merged to main 2026-08-13T10:39:54Z.
- A real post-merge deploy gap (missing worker-exit-status-bridge.py on disk, causing ExecStopPost 203/EXEC crash loops) was found and fixed the same day.
- Follow-on hardening PRs #290/#301/#304/#305 were independently Tier-1 audited and merged, the last minutes before this RCA was dispatched.
- Live-verified: the deployed systemd unit carries the real ExecStopPost hook plus further production hardening beyond PR #249 original scope.

**Conclusion**: no real gap remains attributable to this UMR. `status=killed` is left unchanged (correcting it to `completed` would misattribute later UMRs work to this one). No code fix, no redispatch, no mark-umr-terminal correction. Docs-only change (PROGRESS.md).
